one_liner: C++20 graphics library whose multi-threaded PNG/JPEG codecs beat single-threaded libpng and libjpeg, mostly on mango-encoded files.
what_it_does: MANGO is a large C++20 graphics framework (SIMD math, virtual filesystem, compression, Vulkan text) with its own decoders and encoders for PNG, JPEG and many other formats behind one ImageDecoder / ImageEncoder / Bitmap API. It is not a drop-in for libpng or libjpeg: you load with Bitmap(filename, options) or ImageDecoder(memory, ".png").decode(surface, options) and save with bitmap.save(name, ImageEncodeOptions), and pixel-format conversion happens during decode.
how_it_is_fast: Most of the gap comes from splitting one image across cores. The PNG encoder (ImageEncodeOptions::parallel = true by default) writes a private pLLD chunk and up to 128 independently deflated segments, filtered with SUB only and compressed with ISA-L on x86; the decoder sees pLLD and inflates the segments in parallel on a ConcurrentQueue. The JPEG encoder emits a restart marker per MCU row plus a private APP14 'Mango1' offset table, so its own files, or standard files whose DRI equals one MCU row, get parallel Huffman decoding; other JPEGs decode Huffman serially and only hand iDCT and colour conversion to worker threads. Kernels are SSE2/SSE4.1/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON iDCT, PNG unfilter and colour conversion, chosen at compile time (the default CMake build enables SSE4 only).
when_to_use: You control both ends of the pipeline (game or app assets, caches, screenshots) and can store PNGs and JPEGs written by mango, so later decodes take the parallel pLLD / Mango1 paths
Interactive single-image latency on a many-core desktop, such as opening one large photo or texture, where using every core for one image matters more than total throughput
Camera JPEGs that carry a DRI restart interval of exactly one MCU row, which mango's decoder splits across threads
Projects already on mango (or wanting one C++ API for PNG, JPEG, DDS/KTX, EXR, HEIF, WebP and more) that need fast encode of RGB/RGBA PNGs and accept slightly larger files
when_not_to_use: Decoding arbitrary third-party PNGs: they lack the pLLD chunk, take the single-stream inflate path, and have no published mango numbers, so the 18x decode lead does not carry over
Throughput servers that already decode many images at once on separate threads: the gain comes from per-image threading, not faster single-core code, and no single-threaded mango numbers exist

Untrusted or integrity-sensitive input: the PNG parser skips every chunk CRC, the ISA-L and parallel paths inflate raw deflate after skipping the zlib header (no Adler-32 check), and decode_plld ignores per-segment decompression errors, so corrupt data can decode silently

Smallest files: mango's PNGs were 24% and 19% larger than libpng's in its own tables (SUB filter only, zlib level 4, parallel segments), and its JPEG encoder always writes 4:4:4 with fixed standard Huffman tables
Any build from before commit 2a974fb (2026-09-29) on x86, or before 17c019c on ARM: the default SIMD JPEG decode produced wrong pixels (issue #48), so pin to a fixed commit

integration.form: shared lib (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON by default) or static lib, built with CMake
integration.dependencies: fmt, zlib, libdeflate, zstd, lcms2, ISA-L, LZ4, bzip2 and simdjson per the vcpkg 'base' feature and the apt/brew lines; optional codec libraries (libjxl, OpenJPEG, libwebp, libavif, libheif, LibRaw, jxrlib) and Vulkan/FreeType/HarfBuzz; the benchmark examples also need libjpeg-turbo, libpng and blend2d
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20), CMake 3.19+; documented builds use g++ (apt/pacman), Xcode command-line tools (macOS) and MSVC with vcpkg (Windows); libjxl 0.9+ if JPEG XL is enabled
integration.platforms: x86-64 (default build compiles with SSE4.1/4.2; AVX, AVX2, AVX-512 opt-in), ARM/AArch64 NEON, Linux, macOS, Windows, Emscripten/wasm
integration.thread_safety: not documented; decode and encode default to multithread = true and parallel = true and run work on mango's internal ConcurrentQueue thread pool

gotchas: x86 SIMD JPEG iDCT bug: commit b1061f2 ('Optimize SSE2 iDCT', 2023-10-06) dropped 'r_xmm2 = row5', so the column pass subtracted from a leftover register. The 2026-08-15 refactor copied it into the AVX2 and AVX-512 kernels, and it was fixed in 2a974fb on 2026-09-29 (NEON in 17c019c). Issue #48 reports 254 decoding as 126, with up to 122-128 levels of error on 9-29% of pixels. The README JPEG tables were already in README.md before b1061f2, so the published timings predate the bug.

In png_benchmark, --nomt only clears ImageDecodeOptions::multithread. decode_plld runs whenever a pLLD chunk is present, whatever that flag says, and the mango encode path always uses parallel = true, so the harness cannot produce a single-threaded mango row for its own files.

The JPEG encode rows differ in settings, not only in speed: mango ran at quality 0.70, which scales its quant tables to about 14% of base (roughly libjpeg quality 93, derived from jpeg_encode.cpp), with 4:4:4 sampling. libjpeg ran at quality 95 with jpeg_set_defaults' 4:2:0 sampling and was fed one scanline per call.

Mango's PNGs stay valid for other decoders (segment Adler-32s are combined), but pLLD is a private chunk. Its JPEGs carry RST markers every MCU row and an APP14 'Mango1' table; other decoders ignore both.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: For single-threaded PNG encode, pick fpng or fpnge: in mango's own table fpng (46.0 ms) beat multi-threaded mango (57.2 ms) on the 2560x1600 image. For arbitrary PNGs, pick wuffs, libspng or image-png; for parallel JPEG decode measured against a pinned libjpeg-turbo, pick jpeg-nitro. Pick mango when you write the files yourself and want one image decoded on many cores, or when you already use its C++20 framework.
verified_claims_summary: These are first-party README tables, present by October 2023 and never re-measured, with compiler and flags unstated. PNG on an i7-11800H: on 2560x1600, mango decoded in 3.2 ms against 57.3 ms for libpng, 37.7 for spng and 23.9 for wuffs, and encoded in 57.2 ms against 820.5 for libpng and 46.0 for fpng; on 4833x5875, decode 53.7 vs 379.5 ms and encode 287.0 vs 14051.3 ms. JPEG on an i9-8950HK: on 5184x3456, decode 23.3 vs 197.8 ms for 'libjpeg' (wuffs 185.9) and encode 18.5 vs 70.1 ms. Mango ran multi-threaded against single-threaded baselines, each library was timed once, and both PNG test files are byte-for-byte the size of mango's own output, which means they carry pLLD. The author's own 2023 README text said the JPEG decoder is 'up to three times the speed of jpeglib-turbo' in the best case and about equal in the worst, so the 8.5x table result implies either restart markers in the test file or a baseline other than libjpeg-turbo (not recorded).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-29, vcpkg version 3.8.2) under the zlib license, so copyable, but it is a large framework with many package-manager dependencies rather than a vendorable codec, and its benchmark tables are about three years older than the current code.
